title: BTCMP-18-Module3
prerequisites: With a username and a profile photo Students must:  Discover platforms where the user exists and build a basic profile
outcomes: Objective: Learn how publicly available information can be used to identify individuals and assess the certainty of identification.

levels.title: Introduction level
levels.content:
Welcome to the BTCMP-18 Module 3 Cyber Range Scenario (Identity Investigation).
In this module, you will learn how publicly available information can support the identification of an online persona. 

Using only a username and a profile photo, you will search for platforms where this identity appears and build a simple profile.
The focus is on understanding how open‑source clues connect, while staying within ethical limits: no doxxing, only inference based on what is publicly visible.

You will have 120 minutes to complete the challenge by submitting the appropriate flags requested throughout the lab.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
1. In the topology overview on the right, right-click on **`INV1`** and then click on **`Open GUI`**, and a new pop-up window will appear. 
2. Login into your investigation VM with username **`user`** and password **`Password123`**. 

After successfully connecting to your VM, complete the first flag using the passkey: start.

levels.title: Scenario
levels.content:
**Great — you've successfully connected. I've been waiting for you. We have a new assignment.**

Our analysts have identified an online user operating under the username **johny.skinny**, who appears to have been posting extremist-related content across several social media platforms. 
These activities raise serious security concerns, and we need an initial OSINT assessment.

**On your Desktop, you'll find a folder called CASE_001** containing a text file with target's username and a profile picture. 
The original social media account has already been deleted, so you'll need to search for traces of this identity elsewhere using open-source methods only.

**Your task:** tell us who this person is where else he appear online, and any other related info you can gather.


Clock is running. Good luck."

levels.title: Initial Footprint Discovery
levels.content:
Identify the platform where the username **johny.skinny** has an existing footprint.

Use the pre‑installed OSINT tool **Sherlock** to enumerate accounts.

To run Sherlock, open a terminal and type the command **sherlock** followed by the username you are searching for.

e.g. `sherlock username`

Be cautious of false positives — confirm that any discovered profile truly belongs to the correct individual and not another user with a similar handle. 

You may use the picture at your disposal to correlate your findings.

Your answer should be the social‑media domain name our target has an account on, in the form “http://domain-name.com”.
levels.solution:
* Run Sherlock from the command line using: `sherlock "username"`
* Sherlock will output two social‑media profiles with the same or similar usernames.

Both profiles have posted a photo with scenery. 
Your task is to:
1. Download the photos from both profiles
2. Run dftool to extract their metadata `exiftool name_of_the_image`
3. Run dftool to extract the metadata from the profile picture provided to you. `exiftool name_of_the_image`
4. Compare the camera model and brand with the picture at your disposal


**The correct profile is the one that posted the photo taken with the same camera**

hints.title: Metadata
hints.content: Images contain metadata that can sometimes reveal significant information. Try to download the pictures from the posts and extract their metadata.

levels.title: Deanonymization
levels.content:
“Using the information you have gathered, as well as correlating it with other publicly available data, attempt to determine whether the username **johny.skinny** has ever publicly disclosed a real name. 

Search the social‑media profile from the previous step to identify any traces you can use to move your investigation forward.

Free Hint 1->It’s a common mistake for employees to upload data online for their own convenience, including pages that were never meant to be public. Although these pages are not indexed, it doesn’t mean they aren’t accessible.

Free Hint 2-> Use dirb to enumerate hidden links. Search online for information about dirb’s usage and available arguments.

Your answer should be a full name in the form “First-name Last-name”.
levels.solution:
1. Visit  www.bluefeather.com founded from johny.skinny social media bio email
2. Expose the hidden page using `dirb http://bluefeather.com -X .html,.php,.pdf,.txt`
3. Visit hidden page http://bluefeather.com/staff.html and extract target's full name

hints.title: Look Closer!
hints.content: The target has updated his bio using his corporate email address. Extract the domain from that email and visit it.

hints.title: leaked pages
hints.content:
Search bluefeather.com for any forgotten or leaked pages
Use the dirb tool with the appropriate arguments: `dirb http://bluefeather.com -X .html,.php,.pdf,.txt`

levels.title: Identity Enumeration
levels.content:
Great, we have identified his real name. On staff.html there is also a link to his official social media account. Review his social‑media presence and look for any indicators that might reveal his current place of residence.


One of the most valuable skills in OSINT investigation is the ability to extract location information from a target's social media posts without relying on GPS data or explicit location tags. This technique, known as passive location inference, involves reading post content carefully and identifying geographic clues embedded in everyday language.

Open a text editor on your virtual machine and document every observable detail you can extract from the subject’s publicly visible social media profile. In the next stage, you will have 10 minutes to answer questions based solely on these observations.
Type **report** in the answer field when you are ready.

levels.title: Identity Enumeration Report

questions.text: What is the target’s current city of residence?
Type the full domain name of his personal blog in the format ‘www.domain.com’
What is his Saturday morning activity?
What is his work arrangement? (Remote, In-house, Hybrid, Freelance)

levels.instructions: Based on you report answer the bellow questions

levels.title: Hidden Manifesto
levels.content:
Although his public behavior appears normal, Our analysts insist that he is hiding something. Search more thoroughly for any publicly available content he may have shared that relate to extremism. 

As you noticed on his official social‑media profile, he mentions a personal Blog page. Go check it out! 

Free Hint 1 -> You are looking for evidence that could demonstrate he has shared radical content. This document must contain clear, verifiable indicators of authorship.
Free Hint 2 ->Use ExifTool. Beware that some metadata are hidden! 

Your answer should be the value of a flag in the form “flag-XXXXX-XXXXXXX”.
levels.solution:
1. Use dirb on myblogspot.com — `dirb http://myblogspot.com`. The output will reveal a robots.txt file.

2. In robots.txt, there is a disallow entry: `Disallow: /static/manifest.jpg`.

3. Download the PDF and view hidden metadata using `exiftool -a -u -g1 manifest.jpg`.

4. Capture the flag.

hints.title: Hidden Meta
hints.content: Use `exiftool -a -u -g1 filename.jpg` to reveal hidden metadata

hints.title: Hidden Files
hints.content: search myblogspot.com robots.txt for unindexed content

levels.title: Congratulations
levels.content:
**Congratulations!!!**

You’ve successfully completed the third module, Identity Investigation (People OSINT), within the time limits. 
Return to the LMS to continue the course.
